payload.content: Bug fix on Excalidraw arrow bindings inside Eve. Read the binding update code, reproduce the jump, then make the smallest correct change. Don't rewrite the binding system; bindings carry focus and gap and are recomputed as a bound shape moves.

When you drag a bound shape fast, the arrow's endpoint snaps to the wrong focus point — it jumps to the far side of the box instead of staying near where it was attached. Slow drags are fine. Please find and fix why the focus value goes wrong on fast drags.

summary.text: Bindings store a focus value (a normalized position along the bound edge, roughly -1..1) and a gap. On each pointer move the arrow re-projects onto the shape using focus. If fast drags skip intermediate positions, the focus could be recomputed from the new pointer rather than preserved, flipping sign when the shape crosses the arrow line. Plan: read the binding update path, find where focus is set during drag, reproduce with a synthetic fast-drag, then preserve the stored focus instead of recomputing it mid-drag.

payload.content: I see the suspect. updateBoundElements recomputes focus from the live pointer on every move via determineFocusPoint, and that function's sign depends on which side of the shape center the pointer falls. On a fast drag the shape can cross the arrow's last point between frames, the pointer ends up on the opposite side, and focus flips sign — which reads as the endpoint jumping to the far edge. The stored focus from when the binding was created should be preserved during a drag, not recomputed. Reproducing to confirm the sign flip.

payload.output:
binding created with focus=0.32
slow drag (8 steps): focus stays 0.30..0.34  OK
fast drag (2 steps, shape crosses arrow line): focus recomputed -0.31  <-- SIGN FLIP
endpoint jumped from near-edge to opposite edge as observed

summary.text: Confirmed: the repro shows focus flipping from +0.32 to -0.31 on a fast drag that crosses the arrow line. Root cause is recomputing focus mid-drag from the live pointer. The fix is to preserve the existing endBinding.focus while a shape is being dragged and only recompute it when the binding is first established (or explicitly re-anchored), recomputing gap is fine since gap is unsigned distance. Minimal change: keep focus = arrow.endBinding.focus ?? determineFocusPoint(...) so it only computes when none exists.

payload.name: shell
payload.arguments: {"command":"sed -i '' 's/const focus = determineFocusPoint(arrow, boundShape, pointer)/const focus = arrow.endBinding?.focus ?? determineFocusPoint(arrow, boundShape, pointer)/' lib/canvas/binding.ts"}

payload.content: Fixed. Root cause: updateBoundElements recomputed the binding's focus from the live pointer on every drag frame, and determineFocusPoint's sign depends on which side of the shape center the pointer is on — so a fast drag that crossed the arrow line flipped focus from +0.32 to -0.31 and the endpoint snapped to the opposite edge. The one-line fix preserves the stored endBinding.focus during a drag and only computes it on first bind; gap still updates, and version/versionNonce still bump so the scene re-renders. Tests cover the fast-drag no-flip case. Handoff: the re-anchor gesture (alt-drag to rebind) should explicitly clear focus so it recomputes — left as a follow-up, not in scope here.
